definitions.meaning: A drawing that solves a word problem with bars: one bar for each amount, split into unit boxes, so the relationships in the problem can be seen before calculating.
One equal part of a bar: in the animation Mia has 2 unit boxes and Ben has 3, and every unit box is exactly the same length.
One whole bar split into parts: the class bar of 7 units splits into 3 units of boys and 4 units of girls.
Two bars for the same amount, before and after a change: Mia has 3 units before giving 1 away and 2 units after.
Drawn so lengths stand for amounts faithfully: two units is exactly twice one unit, never a guessed length.

mechanismSteps: Unit bars: every unit is the same length: Mia has 2 units and Ben has 3 units, and the ruler checks that each unit box is the same length.
Before-and-after: the model shows what changed: Mia starts with 3 units, gives 1 unit away to her sister, and the after bar shows 2 units left.
Worked example: part-whole and difference: the whole class bar has 7 units, with 3 units of boys and 4 units of girls, so the difference is 1 unit.
Watch out: bars must be to scale: Sam draws 1 unit and 2 units with boxes that do not match, while the correct 2-unit bar is exactly twice the 1-unit bar.
objectives: Draw a bar model with unit boxes that are all the same length
Use a before-and-after model to show what changed in a problem
Use a part-whole model to split a whole bar into parts and find a difference
Check that bars are to scale before trusting the lengths in a model
subject: math
title: The model method: bar models for word problems

trap.explanation: The bar is treated as a rough sketch rather than a scale model. Every unit box must be exactly the same length: two units is exactly twice one unit. In the animation scene s4 the ruler proves Sam's units do not match, while the correct 2-unit bar is exactly twice the 1-unit bar.
trap.misconception: Drawing unit boxes in any lengths, guessing the sizes.

workedExample: In scene s3, draw the whole class bar first and split it into 7 equal units: 3 units are boys, so the girls are the other 4 units, and diff = 4 − 3 = 1 unit. Read the parts off the model first, then subtract the smaller part from the bigger part.
